data.narrative:
Hexium is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Charlie Jarrott and Jacob Peterson that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a sector peer set of 11 entities: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Of the two valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression was applicable. Peer-Median analysis was not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables in the nuclear energy segment—while 5 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 met narrow stage and valuation-tier filters. Stage-Progression, anchored to the $10M total raised proxy, applied a 2.5x multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $25M.

The triangulated range supported by this single-method analysis is $21M (low) to $29M (high), with a median of $25M. This relatively narrow band reflects the constraint of having only one applicable methodology rather than robust corroboration across multiple approaches. The primary uncertainty stems from the sparse near-peer dataset in nuclear energy at the seed stage; reliance on a sector-wide median would introduce additional noise. Resolution of this valuation range would benefit from either observable comparable transaction data at similar stages or progression toward Series A, which would enable peer-based triangulation.
